clue.text: Carrier in crowd by fire

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece sits next to the other

parts.note: a ruck is a crowd or throng of people
to sack someone is to fire them from a job

explanation.surface: Someone stands in a crowd beside a bonfire, carrying something.
explanation.definitionFit: A backpack is a bag for carrying your belongings on your shoulders.

clue.text: Artist in company raised thanks for this garment

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A painter in a firm gives thanks for a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TA to AT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof coat is worn in wet weather.

clue.text: Luxurious land for a fellow in age, possibly

parts.note: cock is old informal address for a fellow or chap

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A fellow imagines a land of luxury in his old age.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval legend this was an imaginary country of idleness and plenty.

clue.text: Extremely sultry atmosphere up-country

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last
up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: The air is very sultry up-country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AIR to RIA; the hyphen in 'up-country' hides the split.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation with Damascus as its capital.

clue.text: A sailor's revolver at first seems .inapt in prison

indicators.note: in says the earlier letters are put inside the prison word

parts.note: can is slang for prison
the first letter of seems, S, read inside apt, the word inapt split as in apt

explanation.surface: Something seems out of place in a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'inapt' as 'in apt': S goes in APT to make APST, which goes in CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a rotating drum on a ship that sailors turn to haul rope.

clue.text: Writer of four quartets, initially .twice as fly!

indicators.note: twice says the initials are written out two times in a row

parts.note: the poet of Four Quartets is T. S. Eliot, whose initials are T, S and E

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the poet's initials are as light as a fly.
explanation.walkthrough: Four Quartets is T. S. Eliot's poem sequence; 'initially' asks for his initials, TSE, and 'twice' doubles them.
explanation.definitionFit: The African insect that spreads sleeping sickness is a biting fly.

clue.text: Given a break, one hums in class, perhaps

definitions.text: Given a break, one hums in class, perhaps

parts.words: Given a break, one hums in class, perhaps
parts.note: humming here is smelling; once broken open, this prank releases a stench in a classroom

explanation.definitionFit: A small glass capsule that releases a foul smell when broken is a schoolboy prank.

clue.text: Capital toy manufactured without approval

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, wrapping round
manufactured says the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: OK signals approval

explanation.surface: A toy made without permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese seat of government is a capital city.

clue.text: A long time concealing a.deserter's mistakes

indicators.note: concealing says the time word hides the deserter within it

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
a rat is someone who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: An era covering up a deserter's errors.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of printing errors found after publication.

clue.text: Beetle found in tar at foot of craggy cliff

indicators.note: at foot of in a down clue means placed below the other piece

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff
AB is an able seaman, a sailor or tar

explanation.surface: A beetle discovered in tar at the bottom of a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'at foot of' puts AB below SCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A dung beetle held sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Contract makes us careless, losing evidence of 'debts

indicators.note: losing says the longer word drops the named letters

parts.note: incurious means uninterested, not caring to know
IOUs are written notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: A contract that leaves people careless about their debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes IOUS out of INCURIOUS; 'makes us' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract a debt or illness is to bring it upon yourself.

clue.text: Gobbler attracted by the fieldfare?

parts.note: fieldfare is a thrush, but split it as field fare: food eaten out in a field, which draws someone eating outdoors

explanation.definitionFit: Someone eating an outdoor meal in the countryside enjoys food served in a field.

clue.text: Stamp for card

definitions.meaning: stamp as in nature or distinctive mark, as in a man of his stamp
a card is an amusing eccentric person

explanation.definitionFit: Stamp means distinctive nature, and a card is an odd, entertaining person: both senses of the same noun.

clue.text: Flog University tie outside

indicators.note: outside says the tie word wraps round the university letter

parts.note: a knot is a tie in string or rope

explanation.surface: A college tie is being whipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A knout was a Russian whip, and as a verb it means to beat with one.

clue.text: A name mistakenly given to Richard I?

indicators.note: mistakenly says the letters of the next word are set wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the Lionheart was given a wrong name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' rearranges GIVEN to GEVIN after A and N. The question mark marks Richard I as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard I belonged to the Plantagenet house descended from the Counts of Anjou.

clue.text: Adaptable substitute almost appears in live broadcast

indicators.note: appears in says the shortened substitute goes inside the other letters
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ersatz means a substitute or imitation

explanation.surface: A stand-in appears on a live broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ERSATZ to ERSAT; 'broadcast' rearranges LIVE to VILE, and 'appears in' puts ERSAT inside: V-ERSAT-ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to turn to many different tasks or uses with ease.

clue.text: Accent assumed by a walker

definitions.meaning: a regional, especially Irish, way of speaking
a sturdy shoe that a walker puts on

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an Irish lilt in speech and a stout perforated leather shoe for walking.

clue.text: Russian fellow oppressed by our nation's bad weather

indicators.note: oppressed by in a down clue means pressed under, sitting below the other pieces

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, is the British setter's nation
rain is bad weather
Ian is a man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: A Russian man is weighed down by British rain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'oppressed by' puts IAN under UKRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: When this was set Ukraine was part of the Soviet Union, so its people were loosely called Soviet or Russian.

clue.text: Lads hope to reform the plant

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Boys hope a plant will reform them.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily of Greek legend, the flower of the Elysian fields.

clue.text: One who puts up with a native servant

definitions.meaning: in British India a personal servant was called this

explanation.definitionFit: The word means someone who endures, and also a household manservant in colonial India.

clue.text: Low whispering sound made by a philosopher?

indicators.note: made by points to a sound, so the name is as heard spoken

parts.note: Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher murmurs quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: The name Russell and the word for a soft dry sound are said almost alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft crackling noise of leaves or paper moving.

clue.text: New buses crossing' river to dormitory area

indicators.note: crossing says the bus letters stretch across the river letter, which sits inside them
new says the letters are made fresh, in a different arrangement

parts.note: buses read as more than one bus, here two of them side by side

explanation.surface: New buses cross a river on the way to a commuter district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buses' gives two copies of BUS; 'New' rearranges BUSBUS to SUBUBS, and 'crossing' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormitory area is a residential district on a city's edge where commuters sleep.

clue.text: Odds on a river featuring in verse

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds in betting
taken as written
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: Betting odds on a river appear in a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of two long syllables is found in poetry.

clue.text: Two seats for riders here — some dismount 'and embrace

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Riders get off and hug each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h in 'and (for hand) is a cockney touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle built for two people has a saddle for each.

clue.text: A hearing curtailed in the Roman. courts

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail, its last letter, is cut off

parts.note: a trial is a hearing in a law court

explanation.surface: A court hearing in ancient Rome was cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: In a Roman house the central open courtyards were these halls.

clue.text: Lively filly gets away? It's touch and-go

indicators.note: gets away says the filly letter leaves the word

parts.note: frisky means lively and playful
F is the abbreviation for filly in racing form

explanation.surface: A frisky young horse escapes, a precarious moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A risky situation is precarious, its outcome uncertain.

clue.text: Marine 'creature, they say, cut through net

indicators.note: they say means the words are as heard spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: cut through is sawed, and to net is to fish

explanation.surface: Someone describes a sea creature that sliced through a fishing net.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken in a non-rhotic British accent, 'sawed fish' sounds like the marine creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ocean fish with a long flat bill is a sea creature.

clue.text: Figure of girl soldier seen on square

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
GI is an American soldier
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T stands for square

explanation.surface: A girl soldier is spotted on a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: A single numeral from 0 to 9 is a number.

clue.text: Produced whisky, however, and disappeared outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for disappeared wraps round the other piece

parts.note: died, as in a sound that died away and disappeared
still means however or nevertheless

explanation.surface: Someone made whisky and then vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is made by heating a mash and condensing the vapour, a process of purifying spirit.

clue.text: Liberal in good Scottish brotherhood …

indicators.note: in says the Liberal letter goes inside the Scottish word

parts.note: guid is the Scots spelling of good

explanation.surface: A Liberal joins a worthy Scottish fraternity.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval association of craftsmen or merchants was a fellowship of members.

clue.text: … will possibly put down border violence

parts.note: may expresses something that will possibly happen
a hem is the turned border of cloth

explanation.surface: Continuing the brotherhood story: a will might lay down a border, leading to violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' links the pieces, as in writing one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc and violent disorder are what the word describes.

clue.text: "Alarum'd by his ——, the wolf" (Macbeth)

parts.note: a line from Macbeth's dagger speech, where murder is woken by the wolf who keeps watch for it

explanation.definitionFit: The wolf keeps guard for murder, so it is a lookout or watchman.
